original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Whether the no-edge irreducible joint-image bound stays 3 when the off-diagonal pattern space has dimension 4.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package instead answers open question 2 of #6921: the irreducible bound for a complete no-edge pool in pattern dimension 4. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838 and #6921.
bottleneck_link: Side result. The dimension-at-most-3 theorem does not transfer to pattern dimension 4, so a later word argument cannot quote bound 3 there. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet, and the selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the four-cycle pool is proved complete and irreducible at every width at least 4, and the width-6 parity pool is rechecked as reducible. Do not classify all pattern-dimension-4 pools or start paid-rank accounting.
evidence: PROOF.md shows that the four cyclic projectors form a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 and act irreducibly on a four-dimensional joint image at every width at least 4. The same note recomputes the #6838 width-6 parity pool and shows that its five-dimensional image has a four-dimensional invariant kernel. verify.py repeats the finite tables, the F2^4 subspace census, the width-4 through width-8 pool scan, and the negative controls.

ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the case analysis and the package verifier. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 act irreducibly on a joint image of dimension 5 or more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The four-cycle shows that irreducible dimension 4 occurs, so bound 3 fails, but it does not decide whether 4 is an upper bound. The width-6 parity pool has total image 5 and is reducible, so it is not a witness for a larger irreducible image.
open_questions.first_step: Either give one explicit complete no-edge pattern-dimension-4 pool with joint-image dimension at least 5 and a written invariant-subspace check, or prove an upper bound under these same hypotheses.
open_questions.blocked_by: No support reduction in this package bounds the search, and a search that finds no example would not be a proof.
